subject: document-text-extraction
seam_note: The page-classification loop incremented empty_pages and continued, discarding the page number at the exact moment it knew it. commands/ocr/mod.rs::run_gemini_ocr takes a file, so the two halves could never be joined: the system could say 'four pages are scanned' and not which four. kb_ingest.rs:388 refuses only when chunks.is_empty(), i.e. every page unreadable -- the partial case was never the guard's target (its doc comment names the fully-scanned failure it was built for). Fix: extracted chunk_pages() as a pure fn over page texts returning (chunks, unreadable_pages), added format_page_ranges(), persisted ranges into the existing nullable kb_documents.metadata_json (no migration), and the context digest now names pages instead of a count.

subject: quality-gates
seam: src/features/teams/sub_factory/passport/passportModel.ts:16-34 (11 level unions, every one beginning 'none', none carrying a not-assessed member) + app-passport.json (15 dimensions, hand-maintained, no source type defines it)
seam_note: Two passports with opposite failure modes. (1) The ROOT JSON: 15 dimensions of level/tool/skippedByChoice/note. 11 of 15 resolve from structured fields (a tool pointer); 3 hold tool:null which merges 'no tool needed' / 'tool exists, unrecorded' / 'nobody looked'; 1 is skippedByChoice. No `reason` field exists anywhere in it, so absent-with-a-pointer-to-why is inexpressible and skippedByChoice records THAT a skip happened, never what for. One collection-level generatedAt (2026-07-26) for all 15, so evidence age is knowable for 0 of 15. Grep confirms `skippedByChoice` appears in NO source file -- the artifact has no type, no validator, no generator. (2) The TYPED model, which is the stronger finding: every level union starts with 'none' and none has a not-assessed member, the field is non-optional, and passportDerive.ts:9 DOCUMENTS the conflation as intent ('Where there is NO signal the passport shows an explicit gap (null / none)'). The chain completes downstream: derive.ts:233 makes observability a binary over a 5-member union (3 levels unreachable), :253 scores 'none' at 0 of 18, and :268 renders it to the user as an assertion -- 'No error tracking / monitoring connector bound'. An unassessed dimension is therefore published as a definite negative claim about the project. Third asymmetry: evidence fields per dimension are uneven -- tests has 3 (coveragePct, frameworks, criticalPathCovered), ci has 2, security has 1, observability has 0, so the one dimension carrying no evidence pointer is the one whose level cannot be corroborated. And skippedByChoice has no counterpart in the typed model at all, so a deliberate skip recorded in the root passport is DISCARDED at the boundary rather than merely unstructured.
measurable: dimensions whose evidence state resolves from structured fields alone (no prose read)
arm_a: 11 of 15 (shipped JSON schema); 0 of 15 have an individually knowable evidence age
arm_b: 15 of 15 (four-state field: satisfied-with-pointer / in-progress-with-pointer / absent-with-pointer-to-why / explicit unknown); 15 of 15 with a per-dimension date
negative_result: The predicted unreadable-blank population is ABSENT in the JSON -- 0 of 15 carry neither pointer nor note. The discipline is the author's, not the schema's, which is the technique's own convention-not-schema hazard observed as currently benign. The typed model has no such author discipline available to it, which is why the same failure bites there.
structural_fact: The absence state degenerates to a boolean in the JSON and to a definite value ('none') in the types -- two independent shapes of the same error, in one project, neither designed. unknown-is-not-a-value at the type level in 11 places.
instrument_named: add a not-assessed member to the level unions (or make the field optional) and count dimensions holding it; readable before any score or gate changes, and it immediately separates the 'none' blockers that are claims from the ones that are guesses
return_condition: the countable-backlog claim needs two passport generations under the four-state schema to compare; this tree has one

subject: optional-dependency-degradation
note: Census of capability-conditional fallbacks for CLOSING gaps (Worker, IntersectionObserver, ResizeObserver), excluding typeof window/document server guards which are a STABLE absence and belong to the subject original lane. Arm A (tree as-is) vs arm B (technique applied) on three separable claims: C1 branch tests the capability not a proxy 8/8; C2 check present, no unconditional substitute 8/8; C3 branch taken is emitted 0/8. Delta is C3 alone. Instrument self-asserted twice: non-zero population required, and the emission probe must fire elsewhere in the tree (it does).
structural_fact: The check is load-bearing and the emission is not, and conformance tracks consequence rather than diligence. Omitting the capability check crashes on the runtime that lacks it, so 8/8 write it correctly and none uses a version/UA proxy. Omitting the branch signal behaves identically everywhere and fails no test, so 0/8 write it. Result: 8 correct automatic reapers whose firing nobody can observe -- the code cannot be deleted because the doubt one counter would settle has no counter.
instrument_named: emit the branch taken (real capability vs substitute) at each of the 8 seams; the share of sessions taking the substitute is the retirement condition as a number, and answers both is-it-safe-to-delete and is-the-check-even-working
return_condition: once emission exists, re-read the distribution; a share that will not fall means the check drifted, a share at zero means delete the path
commit_note: appended only -- product code untouched; the census ran read-only over tracked sources

subject: module-design
seam: src-tauri/src/engine/runner/credentials.rs:50-83 (ZeroizingFields newtype; Deref+DerefMut to HashMap<String,String>; invariant enforced only in replace() and Drop) + the single mutating use at credentials.rs:826-831
seam_note: ZeroizingFields exists for ONE invariant: no decrypted value is discarded un-zeroized. It enforces it in exactly two places (replace(), Drop) and then implements DerefMut, which forwards every mutating method HashMap has -- none of which scrub. Exactly one caller mutates through the forwarded surface (an insert overwriting access_token after OAuth refresh) and it is CORRECT, because the author hand-rolled the scrub in 4 lines under a comment saying why. That is the finding: the guard left the type and became a convention held by one author's memory. A second such call site silently breaks it, and the wrapper's name promises the scrub is automatic. The function that builds the wrapper also comments that it 'derefs to the underlying HashMap, so the rest of this function reads/mutates it exactly as before' -- the forwarding was adopted to keep the diff small, which is exactly the trade the technique names.
ab: Same probe line `fields.remove("access_token");` through both arms of a faithful standalone reduction (rustc 1.96.1). ARM A (DerefMut present, tree as-is): compiles clean, exit 0 -- decrypted token dropped un-zeroized, no diagnostic. ARM B (DerefMut removed, insert_scrubbed/remove_scrubbed exposed): error[E0596] cannot borrow data in dereference of ZeroizingFields as mutable. Reachable un-scrubbed drop paths: every HashMap mutator -> 0.
return_condition: The product crate does not build in this environment: the tauri build script fails on 'Permission updater:default not found' BEFORE rustc reaches this code, so arm B cannot be shown to compile in the tree. Re-run when that build is green; the change is 3 lines removed + 2 inherent methods + 1 call-site edit.
